newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-DAVENPORT, COETZER ADVANCE EASILY IN OKLAHOMA CITY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-DAVENPORT, COETZER ADVANCE EASILY IN OKLAHOMA CITY.

text.p: OKLAHOMA CITY, Oklahoma, Feb 20 (Reuter) Top seed Lindsay Davenport and second seed Amanda Coetzer raced into the quarter-finals of the IGA Tennis Classic with swift and easy second-round victories on Wednesday.
Olympic champion Davenport needed just 56 minutes to put away Catalina Cristea of Romania 6-2 6-1.
South African Coetzer wasted even less time, blitzing American Meilen Tu 6-1 6-0 in just 45 minutes.
There was one minor upset as Sandra Cacic ousted seventh-seeded fellow American Marianne Werdel Witmeyer 6-4 6-3.

But Witmeyer was lucky even to be playing Wednesday after her first round opponent, Nana Miyhagi of Japan, was forced to retire with a back injury while just one game away from beating the American in straight sets on Tuesday.
Davenport came up with five service breaks in breezing through her first match of the tournament after receiving a first-round bye along with Coetzer.
"I definitely felt in control," Davenport said. "I think I hit the ball really good. We had a lot of good rallies, too."
Davenport next faces the winner of Thursday's match between fifth seed Jennifer Capriati and Kyoko Nagatsuka of Japan.
"It is definitely a tough field and a tough draw for me," she said.
Coetzer, runner-up to Brenda Schultz-McCarthy here last year, will face Frabcesca Lubiani in the quarter-finals after the Italian beat Magdalena Gryzbowska of Poland.
"Last year I did pretty well, but I have struggled here in the past," Coetzer said.
"I am happy with the way I played. She made a few errors. Sometimes the matches go quickly."
